newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile deeply concerned over El Abra accident.
newsitem.headline: Chile deeply concerned over El Abra accident.

text.p: The Chilean government is "tremendously concerned" about safety at El Abra and other large copper mines in Chile after an accident killed four workers Wednesday, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.

Teplizky said he had contradictory reports about what exactly happened at the mine in northern Chile, where four workers were trapped under tonnes of debris after the tunnel they were working collapsed.
"We are tremendously concerned, not only about El Abra but also because so far this year we have had more accidents (in all of Chilean mining) than in all of 1995," Teplizky said.
"We're making a fervent call on companies to reinforce safety codes and set up internal procedures to prevent these things from happening," he told reporters.

The accident at El Abra, owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals, was the third fatal mishap in a Chilean mine this week. A worker at Codelco's El Teniente mine died when he tumbled down a shaft, and another was killed at Codelco's Andina mine.
A team from Chilean mining regulatory agency Sernageomin, led by its mining safety chief Daniel Alcayaga, was at El Abra investigating the accident, state television reported.
Teplizky said he did not want to comment further until he saw Sernageomin's report.
"The information is still very confusing," he said. "We don't want to give any official version yet because we have our doubts about whether things occurred the way the rumors say."

Local television showed trucks and equipment half buried in earth where the tunnel gave way. The workers were loading earth on top of the tunnel, which covered a conveyor belt leading from the mine to the crusher, when the tunnel collapsed without warning, El Abra said in a statement Wednesday.
